'''Morris Marden''' (1905–1991) was an American mathematician.

== Biography ==

He was born on 12 February 1905 in [[East Boston]], United States.<ref name=MardenBio>{{Cite web |title=Morris Marden's Biography |url=https://uwm.edu/math/graduate/resources/history-of-our-graduate-program/morris-mardens-biography/ |access-date=2023-06-19 |website=Mathematical Sciences |language=en-US}}</ref> He was the seventh child of Abram and Fannie B. Marden.<ref name= MardenBio/>

He died in 1991.<ref name= MardenBio/>

== Education ==

He completed his PhD dissertation on ''the Location of the Roots of the Jacobian of Two Binary Forms and of the Derivative of a Rational Function'' under the supervision of [[Joseph L. Walsh]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Morris Marden – The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=8143 |access-date=2023-06-19 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

== Career ==

He is known for the [[Marden's theorem]], which was proven by Jörg Siebeck.{{failed verification|date=June 2023}}<ref name= MardenBio/>

== Bibliography ==

His publications include:<ref>{{Cite web |title=Morris Marden |url=https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/6199663.Morris_Marden |access-date=2023-06-19 |website=www.goodreads.com}}</ref>

* ''Geometry of Polynomials''
* ''The geometry of the zeros of a polynomial in a complex variable''
* ''Geometry of Polynomials. Second Edition. Mathematical Surveys Number 3''
